title: Selectable text comes in whole pieces
statement: Make each selectable piece of text a whole word, phrase, clause or sentence, never a fragment cut mid-word or mid-phrase.
detail: The evaluator's rubric for items where students select parts of a text audits every selectable span, asking whether it is a whole word, phrase, clause or sentence rather than a mid-word fragment or an arbitrary cut that distorts meaning (`shadow/bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/hot_text_evaluation.txt` lines 115-120). A span that begins or ends mid-word, or slices a phrase into a fragment a student can't evaluate on its own, fails the item's clarity outright (lines 122-124).

evidence.quote: is the span a whole word, phrase, clause, or sentence rather than a mid-word fragment or an arbitrary cut that distorts meaning?

**MUST-FAIL** (`clarity_precision = 0.0`) if any selectable span has `is_coherent_unit: NO` (e.g. a span begins or ends mid-word, or slices a phrase so the selectable text reads as a fragment that a student cannot evaluate on its own).
Up to n quotes from a ranked pool of units, the best first, shown in the text's order: whole clauses first (a line and
the rest of its sentence, three lines of one speech at most), then single lines; never a line in `taken` or one the
